# clavis lease config-create

<p class="cli-lead">Create a PostgreSQL or AWS STS dynamic secret config</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis lease config-create [flags]
```

</div>

Describe how to issue credentials: a Postgres server and the role to grant, or an AWS role to assume.

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">Postgres</p>

```sh
clavis lease config-create --host db.internal --database app \
  --username clavis_admin --password "$PGPASSWORD" \
  --grant-role app_readwrite --default-ttl 3600 --max-ttl 86400
```

<p class="cli-example-title">AWS STS</p>

```sh
clavis lease config-create --engine aws --aws-region eu-central-1 \
  --aws-access-key "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" --aws-secret-key "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" \
  --aws-role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/deploy
```

## Details

AWS leases return `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `session_token` and `expiration`. STS credentials can't be renewed; create a new lease.
